scenes.heading: Adding and subtracting decimals
scenes.say: Is zero point six plus zero point seven equal to zero point one three? It's a really common mistake. Let's see how to add and subtract decimals properly.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Dollars, 10-cent and 1-cent coins go in separate piles
scenes.science: Ones, tenths and hundredths go in separate columns
scenes.breaks: money stops at hundredths, but decimals can go further. You just need more columns.
scenes.say: Imagine counting coins in piles: dollars, ten-cent coins and one-cent coins. You'd never mix the piles. Lining up decimal points does the same job. It keeps ones with ones and tenths with tenths. The analogy breaks down because money stops at cents, but decimals can keep going.

scenes.heading: How to do it
steps: Carry or borrow like whole numbers
scenes.say: Here's how. Line up the decimal points. Fill any gaps with zeros. Work from right to left, carrying and borrowing just like with whole numbers. Then bring the decimal point straight down.

scenes.heading: Adding
scenes.question: Work out 12.7 + 4.85 + 9.
scenes.say: Work out twelve point seven plus four point eight five plus nine. Write nine as nine point zero zero. Hundredths add to five. Tenths add to fifteen, so carry one. Ones add to sixteen, so carry again. Tens give two. The answer is twenty-six point five five.
scenes.caption: Work out 12.7 + 4.85 + 9. Write 9 as 9.00. Hundredths add to 5. Tenths add to 15, so carry 1. Ones add to 16, so carry again. Tens give 2. The answer is 26.55.

scenes.heading: Subtracting
scenes.question: Work out 8 − 3.46.
scenes.say: Now eight take away three point four six. Write eight as eight point zero zero. You need to borrow, so eight ones become seven ones, nine tenths and ten hundredths. Then subtract each column. The answer is four point five four. Check by adding back: four point five four plus three point four six is eight.
scenes.caption: Now 8 − 3.46. Write 8 as 8.00. Borrow: 8 ones become 7 ones, 9 tenths and 10 hundredths. Subtract each column. The answer is 4.54. Check by adding back: 4.54 + 3.46 = 8.

scenes.heading: Line up the points, not the ends
scenes.say: The biggest trap is lining up the right-hand ends, like you do with whole numbers. Three point four five plus two point three is five point seven five, not three point six eight.
scenes.caption: The biggest trap is lining up the right-hand ends, like you do with whole numbers. 3.45 + 2.3 is 5.75, not 3.68.

points: Carry and borrow like whole numbers
scenes.say: Quick recap. Line up the points. Add zeros to fill gaps. Carry and borrow just like whole numbers. And zero point six plus zero point seven is one point three, not zero point one three! Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Line up the points. Add zeros to fill gaps. Carry and borrow just like whole numbers. And 0.6 + 0.7 = 1.3, not 0.13! Now try the practice questions!
